doc.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024

title: Skeptical parents and Michigan's range of paths
summary: Rowe explains to parents the many ways to earn a living in music and Michigan's entrepreneurship and technology programs.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Have you ever had to have a discussion with skeptical parents about actually their son or daughter going into this field?

Sure. Yes. Absolutely. And Michigan being a Research 1 institution and obviously an excellent institution for many different types of things, is a place that students often will come and double major, sometimes because they really have a passionate interest in both jazz and something else, and partly because maybe their parents want them to have the — well it’s hard to know which is the back-up degree sometimes, but they want them to have that other degree so that they will be ensured of getting a job when they get out. So when we have those conversations we talk about the myriad ways that students can earn a living in music, and the fact that we have a great diversity of musical offerings for them to follow, paths to follow once they come to school and then we have things like our Entrepreneurship and Leadership Program which is going to help give them business skills. You know between composing, arranging, videogame music, teaching privately, teaching academically in a high school or college, performing — there’s just so many avenues. And then some of them get — end up doing a lot of class work in our Performing Arts Technology degree which is helping them learn all the technology and getting their chops to work in a studio, things like that. So yeah I have those conversations but I think Michigan is pretty well equipped to give students a well- rounded program so they can go out and work.
